questions.q: Which foundational command from Jesus (Matthew 28:19-20) acts as the primary driving force for the growth of the Christian church today?
options: To collect tithes from all nations to build the temple
To isolate themselves in monasteries to maintain purity
To go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing and teaching them
To engage in political wars to conquer surrounding nations
questions.explain: The Great Commission instructs believers to "Go therefore and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them... and teaching them to observe all that I have commanded you." This is the basis of global evangelism and church growth.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: According to the CRS syllabus, which of the following is a modern mark or method of growth in the Christian church today?
options: Organizing crusades, revivals, vigils, and prayer meetings
Forcing people to convert through government laws
Banning members from talking to non-believers
Refusing to accept new members into the congregation
questions.explain: Modern church growth is often characterized by dynamic spiritual gatherings such as organizing crusades, revivals, night vigils, prayer meetings, and the occurrence of miracles, which attract people to the faith.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: In the early days of church growth (Acts 2:47), while the disciples praised God and had favor with all the people, who was responsible for adding to their number day by day?
options: The Roman Emperor
The High Priest
The Lord
Peter
questions.explain: Acts 2:47 explicitly states: "...praising God and having favor with all the people. And the Lord added to their number day by day those who were being saved."
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: To foster unity among various Christian groups in Nigeria, a major umbrella organization was established. What does the acronym CAN stand for?
options: Catholic Alliance of Nigeria
Christian Association of Nigeria
Council of Anglican Nations
Christians Arise Network
questions.explain: CAN stands for the Christian Association of Nigeria. It is an umbrella organization that promotes unity, peace, and cooperation among different Christian denominations in the country.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: What does the term "Inter-denominational" mean in the context of church activities today?
options: Activities limited strictly to one specific church branch
A conflict or debate between two different religions
Activities that involve people from different Christian denominations coming together to worship or work
A rule that forbids Christians from attending other churches
questions.explain: Inter-denominational refers to actions, organizations, or services that cross the boundaries of individual denominations (like Baptists, Methodists, Pentecostals) to unite them for a common Christian purpose.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: In teaching about Christian giving to support the church and those in need (2 Corinthians 9:6-7), Paul wrote that God loves a ________ giver.
options: reluctant
wealthy
cheerful
forceful
questions.explain: 2 Corinthians 9:7 states: "Each one must give as he has decided in his heart, not reluctantly or under compulsion, for God loves a cheerful giver."
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: To foster unity in the church, Paul encouraged believers in Philippians 2:3 to do nothing from selfish ambition or conceit. Instead, what attitude should they have?
options: They should in humility count others more significant than themselves.
They should strive to become the wealthiest in the congregation.
They should debate until one person wins the argument.
They should ignore anyone who disagrees with them.
questions.explain: Paul emphasizes humility as the key to unity, writing: "Do nothing from selfish ambition or conceit, but in humility count others more significant than yourselves."
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: In James 2:14-18, a specific teaching is given to show how Christians should live out their unity and care for one another. James declares that faith by itself, if it does not have works, is ________.
options: still valid
dead
asleep
imperfect but acceptable
questions.explain: James 2:17 makes this profound statement: "So also faith by itself, if it does not have works, is dead." Genuine faith must be accompanied by practical actions like caring for the needy.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: According to Matthew 5:16, how should a Christian live among non-Christians in their community?
options: They should hide their faith so they are not persecuted.
They should condemn non-Christians publicly every day.
They should let their light shine so others may see their good works and glorify God.
They should isolate themselves in Christian-only neighborhoods.
questions.explain: Jesus taught, "In the same way, let your light shine before others, so that they may see your good works and give glory to your Father who is in heaven."
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: In 1 Peter 3:8-17, what is the recommended attitude for Christians when facing persecution or insult from non-believers?
options: To retaliate physically and defend their honor
To sue the offenders in the local courts immediately
To not repay evil for evil, but on the contrary, to bless them
To insult them back to prove they are strong
questions.explain: 1 Peter 3:9 instructs: "Do not repay evil for evil or reviling for reviling, but on the contrary, bless, for to this you were called, that you may obtain a blessing."
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: According to James 1:12, what reward is promised to the Christian who remains steadfast and endures trials and persecution from the world?
options: The crown of life
Immense earthly riches
Total political power
Exemption from paying taxes
questions.explain: James 1:12 says: "Blessed is the man who remains steadfast under trial, for when he has stood the test he will receive the crown of life, which God has promised to those who love him."
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: What is the general biblical teaching regarding a Christian's attitude toward non-believing government authorities, assuming they do not force the Christian to disobey God?
options: Christians should actively plot to overthrow them.
Christians should obey the laws of the land, pay their taxes, and live as good citizens.
Christians should ignore all civil laws because they only answer to God.
Christians should refuse to pay taxes to a non-believing ruler.
questions.explain: Based on teachings from Jesus (paying taxes to Caesar) and Paul (Romans 13), Christians are instructed to be peaceful, law-abiding citizens and submit to governing authorities as a testimony to their faith.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: What is the definition of "peaceful co-existence" in a diverse society?
options: Living in harmony, tolerance, and peace with people of different beliefs and backgrounds
Forcing everyone in the community to practice the exact same religion
Avoiding all contact with anyone who does not share your faith
Living together but constantly debating and arguing over differences
questions.explain: Peaceful co-existence refers to the ability of people from different religions, cultures, or backgrounds to live together in a community harmoniously, with mutual respect and tolerance.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: Which two brothers in the Old Testament provided an excellent example of desiring peaceful co-existence by embracing and forgiving each other after years of bitter enmity over a stolen blessing? (Genesis 33)
options: Cain and Abel
Joseph and Benjamin
Isaac and Ishmael
Esau and Jacob
questions.explain: In Genesis 33:4, despite Jacob's fears of revenge, "Esau ran to meet him and embraced him and fell on his neck and kissed him, and they wept." This act brought peaceful reconciliation.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: In the New Testament, Paul wrote a letter to Philemon encouraging peaceful co-existence, forgiveness, and settlement of disputes. Who was the other party involved in this dispute with Philemon?
options: Silas, his business partner
Onesimus, his runaway slave who had become a Christian
Peter, who had disagreed with him over Jewish laws
Barnabas, his former missionary companion
questions.explain: Paul sent Onesimus, a runaway slave, back to his master Philemon, urging Philemon to receive him not as a slave but "as a beloved brother." This is a powerful demonstration of reconciliation.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: Which of the following represents a practical demonstration of how Christians can show a desire for peaceful co-existence with non-Christians today?
options: Calling for dialogue, tolerance, and the amicable settlement of disputes
Mocking the religious traditions of other faiths publicly
Refusing to do business with anyone who isn't a Christian
Using violence to protect church property
questions.explain: The syllabus emphasizes that Christians show a desire for peace through "dialogue, tolerance, forgiveness, reconciliation or settlement of disputes."
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: In promoting peaceful co-existence between Christians and Muslims in communities, it is often noted that both religions trace their origins to one common patriarch. Who is this father of faith? (Gen. 16, 21)
options: Moses
David
Abraham
Noah
questions.explain: Both Christianity (through Isaac) and Islam (through Ishmael) recognize Abraham as a foundational father of their faith. Recognizing this shared heritage can serve as a basis for mutual respect and peaceful co-existence.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: Which of the following actions demonstrates a lack of unity and hinders the growth of the Christian church today?
options: Organizing inter-denominational crusades
Promoting ethnic discrimination and selfish ambition among members
Praying fervently for one another
Contributing money to support the less privileged
questions.explain: The CRS syllabus addresses issues that threaten unity. Discrimination based on tribe, ethnicity, or social class, along with selfish ambition, directly opposes Christ's prayer for unity in John 17 and Paul's commands in Philippians 2.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: In Galatians 6:1, Paul provides instruction on how to restore a brother who is caught in a sin to maintain church unity. How should spiritual believers handle such a situation?
options: They should gossip about him to warn others.
They should restore him in a spirit of gentleness, while keeping watch on themselves.
They should publicly humiliate him during Sunday service.
They should physically drive him out of the church building.
questions.explain: Paul emphasizes compassionate discipline: "Brothers, if anyone is caught in any transgression, you who are spiritual should restore him in a spirit of gentleness. Keep watch on yourself, lest you too be tempted."
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: Christian student organizations in schools (such as the Fellowship of Christian Students, FCS) are primarily established to achieve what goal?
options: To train students on how to fight against non-believers
To help students pass their promotional examinations using secret answers
To promote moral uprightness, Bible study, and Christian fellowship among youths
To protest against the rules of the school principal
questions.explain: Christian organizations in educational institutions foster spiritual growth, unity among diverse believers, moral discipline, and biblical knowledge in students.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: If a secular, non-believing authority issues a command that directly forces a Christian to commit a sin clearly forbidden by God, what is the biblical standard for the Christian's response? (cf. Acts 5:29)
options: They must obey the human authority, as God will understand the pressure.
They must respectfully obey God rather than men, accepting whatever consequences may follow.
They must declare war on the local government.
They should lie to the authority to avoid trouble.
questions.explain: While Christians are commanded to obey the government (Romans 13), the ultimate authority is God. As Peter declared before the Sanhedrin: "We must obey God rather than men" when the two conflict.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: An example of desiring peaceful co-existence in the Bible is found in Genesis 26:26-29, when King Abimelech approached Isaac. Why did the Philistine king initiate this meeting?
options: To declare war because Isaac had grown too wealthy
To make a peace covenant with Isaac, acknowledging that the Lord was clearly with him
To sell a piece of land to Isaac at an expensive price
To force Isaac to worship Philistine idols
questions.explain: Abimelech told Isaac, "We see plainly that the Lord has been with you. So we said, let there be a sworn pact between us... that you will do us no harm, just as we have not touched you..." This demonstrated a desire for peaceful co-existence based on mutual respect.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: In Philippians 4:18, Paul thanks the Philippian church for the financial support they sent him through Epaphroditus. How does Paul describe their Christian giving?
options: As a legal requirement they finally fulfilled
As a fragrant offering, a sacrifice acceptable and pleasing to God
As a down payment for their heavenly mansions
As a bribe to the Roman guards
questions.explain: Paul frames their financial generosity in priestly terms: "I am well supplied, having received from Epaphroditus the gifts you sent, a fragrant offering, a sacrifice acceptable and pleasing to God."
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: To teach unity through impartiality, James gives an example (James 2:1-4) of two men walking into a church assembly. What two extremes of society did these men represent?
options: A religious Jew and a pagan Gentile
A master and a runaway slave
A man with a gold ring in fine clothing, and a poor man in shabby clothing
A Roman soldier and a Jewish tax collector
questions.explain: James rebukes favoritism by setting up this scenario: "For if a man wearing a gold ring and fine clothing comes into your assembly, and a poor man in shabby clothing also comes in..." Believers must not show partiality.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: Paul reminds Christians of the ultimate reason for submitting to constituted authorities in Romans 13:5. It is not only to avoid God's wrath but also for the sake of what?
options: Personal financial gain
Political ambition
Conscience
Earning favor with the emperor
questions.explain: Romans 13:5 states: "Therefore one must be in subjection, not only to avoid God's wrath but also for the sake of conscience." Good citizenship is a moral duty for a believer.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: In Mark 16:15-16, which is known as part of the Great Commission, what does Jesus state will happen to the one who believes and is baptized, compared to the one who does not believe?
options: Whoever believes will be wealthy, but whoever does not will be poor.
Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved, but whoever does not believe will be condemned.
Whoever believes will become a priest, but whoever does not will be a servant.
Whoever believes will never get sick, but whoever does not will face illness.
questions.explain: Jesus explicitly stated the spiritual consequences of the gospel message: "Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved, but whoever does not believe will be condemned."
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: In Galatians 6:2, Paul provides a clear way for Christians to maintain unity and practically show love for one another. He says, "Bear one another's burdens, and so fulfill the law of ______."
options: Moses
the Prophets
Christ
the Church
questions.explain: By helping fellow believers with their struggles, Christians fulfill "the law of Christ," which is grounded entirely in self-sacrificial love.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: In Matthew 5:23-24, Jesus taught about the priority of peaceful co-existence. What did He say a person must do if they are offering a gift at the altar and remember that their brother has something against them?
options: Offer the gift quickly and then go apologize.
Leave the gift before the altar, first be reconciled to their brother, and then come and offer the gift.
Keep the gift and never speak to the brother again.
Give half the gift to the brother to appease his anger.
questions.explain: Jesus heavily prioritized interpersonal reconciliation over religious ritual, instructing believers to resolve disputes and make peace before offering their worship to God.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: When addressing Christian living among non-Christians, the Apostle Peter encourages believers to have unity of mind, sympathy, brotherly love, a tender heart, and a humble mind (1 Peter 3:8). What is the primary purpose of living this way?
options: To ensure they win every political election in their town
To inherit a blessing from God and be a good testimony to unbelievers
To prove that they are more intelligent than the rest of society
To avoid paying civil taxes to the Roman authorities
questions.explain: Peter urges believers to exhibit these gentle and unifying traits so they might "inherit a blessing" (1 Pet 3:9) and live honorably among non-believers, showing the reality of their faith.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: The story of Philemon and Onesimus represents a profound lesson on Christian forgiveness and peaceful co-existence. What was the original relationship between these two men before Paul intervened?
options: They were rival kings of neighboring territories.
Onesimus was Philemon's runaway slave.
They were brothers fighting over an inheritance.
Philemon was a Roman judge and Onesimus was a thief.
questions.explain: Onesimus had been a slave who ran away from his master, Philemon. After converting to Christianity, Paul sent him back, urging Philemon to receive him not as a slave, but as a beloved Christian brother.
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)

questions.q: In 1 Peter 1:6-9, Peter addresses Christians going through various trials and persecutions. He explains that these trials have a specific purpose: to test the genuineness of their ____________.
options: intelligence
faith
wealth
physical strength
questions.explain: Peter compares their trials to a refining fire: "so that the tested genuineness of your faith—more precious than gold that perishes though it is tested by fire—may be found to result in praise and glory and honor at the revelation of Jesus Christ."
questions.exam: BECE CRS: Christian Religious Studies: New Testament Part 2 (Paper 2)
questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies

questions.q: What practical outcome should arise from Christians demonstrating love, tolerance, and a desire for peaceful co-existence with their Muslim neighbors in Nigeria?
options: A constant battle for supremacy over community resources
A harmonious society devoid of religious violence and ethnic tension
The establishment of a nationwide Christian state
The total separation of communities by religious beliefs
questions.explain: The ultimate goal of peaceful co-existence taught in the CRS syllabus is for believers to interact harmoniously with non-believers (including those of other faiths like Islam), preventing religious crises and promoting peace and national development.
